# SciFact ×10 (latency at 50k rows)

*Generated by `scripts/gen_bench_pages.py` from the `oml-bench/1` results in `eval/bench/results/`; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with `python scripts/gen_bench_pages.py`, and CI fails when this page differs from what it writes.*

Suite `beir-scifact-x10`, data `beir/scifact/test x10 (ir_datasets 0.6.3)`: 8,825 memories, 300 queries; a method marked sampled asked a seeded subset, named in its row. Measured 2026-11-04 on commit `9a6a0d0`; build release, host 8 vCPU / 15 GB, postgres 17.9.

[All suites](index.md)

## Limits of this run

- SciFact's abstracts and nine copies with 10% of words replaced, 51,830 memories written to one workarea, for latency at scale; qrels name the original copy only, so quality is not comparable to beir-scifact. k 100, no token budget. 8,825 of the 51,830 rows written were promoted when it ran, so the scope held those: approval through review next slowed with the queue (FR-87).
- SciFact's abstracts and nine copies with 10% of words replaced, 51,830 memories written to one workarea, for latency at scale; qrels name the original copy only, so quality is not comparable to beir-scifact. k 100, no token budget. 8,825 of the 51,830 rows written were promoted when it ran, so the scope held those: approval through review next slowed with the queue (FR-87). Asked with k 10, the size an agent asks, to measure latency at that k; recall@100 reads the shorter list.
